title: Understanding and Mitigating the Fragility of Self-Rewarding Optimization
abstract: arXiv:2611.28582v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Self-rewarding optimization (SRO) promises to improve language models by enabling them to generate their own reward signals. Yet when and how SRO succeeds or fails remains poorly understood. We reveal that SRO is fundamentally fragile: even seemingly benign perturbations to training prompts can corrupt the self-generated preference signal and trigger iterative collapse. We demonstrate this through two prompt-level attacks that serve as controlled stress tests: a Re-Ranking attack that concentrates training on prompts where self-reward diverges from an oracle, and a Preamble attack that learns short prefixes inflating self-reward without any gain in oracle quality. translated_title: 理解并缓解自我奖励优化的脆弱性
translated_abstract: 自我奖励优化（SRO）有望通过让语言模型生成自身的奖励信号来改进模型。然而，SRO何时以及如何成功或失败仍然缺乏深入理解。我们揭示出SRO本质上是脆弱的：即使对训练提示词进行看似良性的扰动，也可能破坏自我生成的偏好信号并引发迭代崩溃。我们通过两种提示词层面的攻击（作为可控压力测试）来证明这一点：一是“重新排序”攻击，它将训练集中在自我奖励与参考标准产生分歧的提示词上；二是“前导词”攻击，它通过学习简短的前缀来抬高自我奖励，而模型实际质量却没有任何提升。为解释这些攻击为何能够成功，我们引入了自我奖励保真度（SRF），这是一个量化自我评估奖励与参考标准奖励之间在策略上一致性的指标。我们证明SRF可以作为自我监督可靠性的诊断信号，并且受控的SRF扰动……
tldr: 该论文揭示了自我奖励优化（SRO）本质上是脆弱的——微小的提示词扰动即可破坏其自我生成的偏好信号并引发迭代崩溃，并提出自我奖励保真度（SRF）指标作为诊断自我监督可靠性的信号，以理解和缓解这种脆弱性。
en_tdlr: This paper reveals that self-rewarding optimization is fundamentally fragile—even benign prompt perturbations can corrupt its self-generated preference signals—and introduces self-reward fidelity (SRF) as a diagnostic metric to understand and mitigate this fragility.
